info.title: Language decisions
info.text:
High-level languages hide many hardware details.

Low-level languages expose processor operations.

The project requirements should guide the choice.

Challenge: Choose a level for a school app that needs frequent updates. Explain why.

A strong explanation names a characteristic and shows how it meets a requirement. A language name alone is often not enough.

info.title: Representations
info.text:
Source code is the programmer’s representation.

Assembly uses mnemonic instructions.

Machine code contains encoded processor instructions.

Challenge: Explain why assembly and machine code are both low-level.

The same binary sequence need not mean the same instruction on another architecture. Compatibility cannot be assumed.

info.title: Translator choices
info.text:
Compilers process source before the translated program runs.

Interpreters process source during execution.

Neither approach removes the need to test.

Challenge: Which route supports quick testing of frequent source edits? Why?

When comparing two approaches, make paired points. Explain what each does rather than listing unrelated advantages.

info.title: IDE evidence
info.text:
Editor features help create readable source.

Diagnostics report detected problems.

Debugging tools help inspect execution.

Challenge: Which tools would help you find why a total changes incorrectly?

The IDE offers facilities. The programmer uses their evidence to decide what change to make.

info.title: Interpreting a trace
info.text:
A trace records the effect of each instruction.

Stored values and the working value are different.

Predict before checking the result.

Challenge: Trace 5 + 8, then subtract 4. What are the two results?

The arithmetic trace applies the idea of instruction order. You do not need to memorise an extra assembly instruction set for J277.

info.title: Writing an explanation
info.text:
Read the requirement before choosing a feature.

Name a relevant characteristic.

Explain its effect on the stated problem.

Challenge: Improve “Use an IDE because it is good” with one specific example.

Use the marks as a guide to the number of distinct points. Correct terminology helps, but the link to the scenario matters too.
